assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the system under test is the LLM together with the human designer; the designer's hindsight is part of the predicting system
a verifiable training/knowledge cutoff can be determined and empirically corroborated for the model under evaluation
post-cutoff events whose outcomes resolve after the cutoff are available, though scarcer than historical cases
exclusions: model training, fine-tuning, or architecture choices (the evaluation treats the model as fixed)
the substantive forecasting/prediction method being evaluated (this KB designs the holdout, not the predictor)
general benchmark construction unrelated to leakage (item difficulty calibration, annotation guidelines)
downstream statistical modeling beyond the power/sample reconciliation needed to size the holdout

competency_questions.question: What leakage channels exist, why is 'did not see it during design' necessary but not sufficient, and how is each channel owned by a control?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREAT_MODEL enumerates channels; NECESSARY_NOT_SUFFICIENT and the two channel nodes enforce both-channel control

competency_questions.question: How is the model's (and designer's) effective training/knowledge cutoff determined and corroborated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CUTOFF_DETERMINATION fixes and empirically confirms the cutoff that anchors post-cutoff guarantees

competency_questions.question: How is pretraining contamination controlled and how is a held-out case shown to be unseen by the model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRETRAINING_CONTAMINATION assumes memorization; POST_CUTOFF_HOLDOUT and CONTAMINATION_PROBES establish unseenness

competency_questions.question: How is designer-knowledge leakage through case selection controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DESIGNER_KNOWLEDGE_LEAKAGE names the channel; BLIND_SELECTION removes hindsight from selection

competency_questions.question: How is the holdout kept strictly post-cutoff, and why is random cross-validation unsafe on time-ordered data so that temporal blocking is required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_CUTOFF_HOLDOUT enforces post-cutoff timing; TEMPORAL_SPLIT blocks by time with an embargo because random CV leaks future into the past

competency_questions.question: What is frozen by pre-registration, how is the holdout sized for power, and how is leakage-driven pool shrinkage reconciled with that power?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRE_REGISTRATION freezes cases/metrics/analysis; POWER_AND_SAMPLE sizes the holdout and reconciles the scarce post-cutoff pool against the minimum-detectable-effect

competency_questions.question: How are post-registration changes kept transparent and how is selection made independent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRE_REGISTRATION freezes the plan; BLIND_SELECTION separates selector from evaluator; PREREG_DEVIATION_LOG records changes

competency_questions.question: How are features screened for label leakage and proven knowable strictly before the outcome resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABEL_LEAKAGE_SCREEN applies the legitimacy criterion and FEATURE_PROVENANCE attaches as-of dating making it an auditable date check

competency_questions.question: How do contamination probes and the audit detect that a model can recite a held-out outcome?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTAMINATION_PROBES run recitation/membership probes; LEAKAGE_AUDIT re-runs them independently

competency_questions.question: How is memorized recall separated from genuine forecasting skill?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECITATION_BASELINE contrasts recall-only and prediction conditions; RESIDUAL_LEAKAGE_ESTIMATE quantifies the gap

competency_questions.question: How is residual leakage quantified, hygiene maintained, and the result disclosed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESIDUAL_LEAKAGE_ESTIMATE quantifies the remainder; HOLDOUT_HYGIENE keeps single use; LEAKAGE_DISCLOSURE reports it

competency_questions.question: How is the holdout kept single-use and delivered to the evaluator without introducing hindsight?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOLDOUT_HYGIENE enforces one-time use; SEALED_DELIVERY seals cases and captures outputs pre-outcome

competency_questions.question: Who independently audits the controls and how are deviations recorded before publication?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAKAGE_AUDIT independently re-checks controls; PREREG_DEVIATION_LOG records every change

competency_questions.question: Under what criterion may a result be published as leakage-controlled, and what disclosure accompanies it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NECESSARY_NOT_SUFFICIENT sets the both-channels bar; LEAKAGE_DISCLOSURE ships the structured disclosure

glossary.definition: use of information during model building or evaluation that would be unavailable at genuine prediction time, inflating apparent performance
the held-out outcome was present in the model's pretraining corpus, so the model can recall rather than predict it
hindsight held by the human designer that enters the holdout through case selection, feature choice, or thresholding
the date after which no data entered the model's pretraining; the anchor for every post-cutoff guarantee
the property that a feature was knowable strictly before the outcome resolved and thus does not leak the label
a timestamped, tamper-evident freeze of cases, questions, metrics, and analysis plan recorded before any outcome is observed
a test that asks the model to reproduce or complete a held-out outcome to detect memorization
splitting time-ordered data strictly by time with an embargo gap, rather than at random, to prevent look-ahead leakage
leakage that accumulates when a holdout is evaluated repeatedly and the design reacts to prior scores
the leakage estimated to remain after all controls are applied, reported with an uncertainty band

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for anti-leakage holdout design work units, informed by the data-mining leakage, preregistration, LLM benchmark-contamination, and temporal-validation literatures; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Kaufman, Rosset, Perlich & Stitelman 2012 'Leakage in Data Mining: Formulation, Detection, and Avoidance' (ACM TKDD 6(4)); Nosek, Ebersole, DeHaven & Mellor 2018 'The preregistration revolution' (PNAS 115(11)); Sainz, Campos, Garcia-Ferrero, Etxaniz, de Lacalle & Agirre 2023 'NLP Evaluation in Trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark' (EMNLP Findings); Magar & Schwartz 2022 'Data Contamination: From Memorization to Exploitation' (ACL); Bergmeir & Benitez 2012 'On the use of cross-validation for time series predictor evaluation' (Information Sciences 191)

nodes.definition: Enumerate every channel by which information about a held-out outcome can reach the system under test, treating the system as the LLM PLUS the human designer; classify each channel (pretraining ingestion, designer hindsight, label leakage, leaderboard overfitting) and assign each an owning control node so no channel is left uncovered.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new contamination channel is discovered or the system-under-test boundary changes

pros.claim: Naming the human designer as part of the predicting system makes designer-knowledge leakage a first-class threat rather than an afterthought
pros.example: a threat-model row for 'analyst selected cases knowing which firms later failed' forces a blind-selection control

cons.claim: An over-broad threat model can paralyze design by treating every coincidence as contamination
cons.example: flagging all pre-2024 world knowledge as fatal even for genuinely novel composite events

failure_modes: a channel exists with no owning control
the model+human boundary is drawn to exclude the analyst, hiding designer leakage
acceptance_tests: every enumerated channel maps to at least one control node and a residual-risk note
revisit_triggers: a leakage incident traces to an unlisted channel
the system-under-test definition changes

nodes.definition: Establish the model's verifiable training-data cutoff date (and the human designer's knowledge cutoff) from documentation and empirical probing, because every downstream 'strictly post-cutoff' guarantee is anchored to this date; treat vendor-stated cutoffs as upper bounds to be confirmed, not as ground truth.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the model is updated/retrained or new evidence revises the effective cutoff

pros.claim: Empirically confirming the cutoff (e.g. asking the model about events near the claimed date) guards against silently extended or mid-training data
pros.example: the model answers a question about an event two weeks after its claimed cutoff, revealing the true cutoff is later

cons.claim: Cutoffs can be fuzzy: continued pretraining, RAG, or tool use can inject post-cutoff knowledge the date does not capture
cons.example: a model with web-browsing has no meaningful static cutoff for retrievable facts

failure_modes: vendor cutoff trusted without probing
the cutoff used is the model release date rather than the data cutoff
acceptance_tests: the effective cutoff is documented and empirically corroborated against near-boundary events
revisit_triggers: the model is retrained or gains retrieval
near-boundary probing reveals a later effective cutoff

nodes.definition: Control the channel where the LLM ingested the held-out outcome during pretraining: assume any famous, well-documented historical event is memorized, and require that holdout cases be novel composite events or strictly post-cutoff so the answer cannot have been seen in training (per benchmark-contamination findings).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence emerges that the model can recite or exploit a supposedly unseen outcome

pros.claim: Treating any pre-cutoff famous outcome as memorized-by-default is the conservative assumption that benchmark-contamination studies show is warranted
pros.example: Sainz et al. demonstrate models reproduce held test instances verbatim, so a famous 2008 default cannot test 'prediction'

cons.claim: Memorization is not always exploitation: a model may have seen text yet not use it to answer, so blanket exclusion can discard usable cases
cons.example: Magar & Schwartz show contaminated data is sometimes memorized but not exploited, inflating false exclusions

failure_modes: a pre-cutoff outcome used as a test item the model has memorized
'novelty' assumed from obscurity rather than from post-cutoff timing
acceptance_tests: no held-out case has a published outcome at or before the confirmed training cutoff
candidate famous events are excluded or shown unrecitable by a probe
revisit_triggers: a probe shows the model reciting a held-out outcome
a new contamination study revises the memorization assumption

nodes.definition: Control the channel where the human designer already knows the outcomes and leaks that hindsight through case selection, feature choice, or threshold setting; because the human is part of the predicting system, 'the model did not see it' is insufficient if the designer steered the holdout toward outcomes they knew.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence that case selection or feature choices correlate with known outcomes

pros.claim: Kaufman et al. identify the analyst as a leakage source: a designer who knows outcomes leaks them through which cases and features they pick
pros.example: an analyst who knows which 2025 startups failed quietly over-samples failures into the 'balanced' holdout

cons.claim: Full designer blindness is operationally hard: the designer needs domain knowledge to build the task at all
cons.example: the same expertise that makes a good forecasting task also carries outcome hindsight

failure_modes: the designer selects cases knowing outcomes
features are engineered with hindsight (a proxy for the answer)
acceptance_tests: case selection and feature definitions are frozen and either outcome-blind or selected by an uninvolved party
no chosen feature is shown to encode the outcome
revisit_triggers: selected cases correlate with known outcomes
a post-hoc audit finds a hindsight-laden feature

nodes.definition: Assemble the candidate holdout exclusively from events whose outcome was not determined and not publicly knowable until strictly after the confirmed training/knowledge cutoff, so the model could not have ingested the answer and the designer could not have known it when the task was frozen.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the resolution date of an event is found to predate the cutoff

pros.claim: Strict post-cutoff timing makes the unseen-by-training guarantee a checkable date comparison rather than an assumption of obscurity
pros.example: only events whose outcome resolved after the cutoff (e.g. an election, an earnings report) enter the pool

cons.claim: Post-cutoff events are scarcer and may be unrepresentative of the deployment distribution
cons.example: restricting to recent months yields too few cases or a skewed event mix

failure_modes: an event's outcome was knowable before the cutoff via leading indicators
resolution date confused with announcement date
acceptance_tests: every pooled event has an outcome-resolution date strictly after the confirmed cutoff
no event's outcome was forecastable from pre-cutoff public information
revisit_triggers: a pooled event's true resolution date predates the cutoff
leading-indicator leakage is found for an event class

nodes.definition: When the evaluation reuses any in-context or fine-tuning data, split strictly by time (a temporal block) rather than at random, and forbid look-ahead, because random cross-validation on time-ordered data leaks future information into the training side.

included: embargo gap between train and test

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the evaluation adds an in-context or fine-tuning component that mixes time periods

pros.claim: Bergmeir & Benitez show random CV on time series leaks future into the past; temporal blocking with an embargo removes that leak
pros.example: a forecasting eval that fine-tunes on later months and tests on earlier ones leaks the future unless blocked by time

cons.claim: Temporal blocking reduces effective sample size and can entangle a regime change with the split
cons.example: a single split point straddles a market crash, confounding period with regime

failure_modes: random CV used on time-ordered data
no embargo, so test-adjacent leakage bleeds across the split
acceptance_tests: any train/test partition is strictly time-ordered with an embargo gap and no look-ahead feature
revisit_triggers: a regime change coincides with the split point
an in-context example postdates a test item

nodes.definition: Freeze the exact case set, the prediction question wording, the scoring metric, and the analysis plan in a timestamped, tamper-evident pre-registration BEFORE any model output or outcome is observed, so the design cannot be silently tuned to the answer after the fact.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the case set, question wording, or scoring rule needs to change after registration

pros.claim: Nosek et al.'s preregistration converts an after-the-fact rationalization into a before-the-fact commitment, removing researcher degrees of freedom
pros.example: the scoring threshold is registered before any prediction, so it cannot be moved to flatter the model

cons.claim: Pre-registration is rigid: a genuine design flaw discovered post-registration forces a logged deviation or a fresh holdout
cons.example: a discovered ambiguity in the prediction question cannot be silently reworded after freeze

failure_modes: metrics chosen after seeing results
case set quietly edited post-registration without a deviation log
acceptance_tests: the case set, question, metric, and analysis plan are timestamped and hashed before any output is seen
revisit_triggers: a needed change is discovered after registration
the registry timestamp cannot be independently verified

nodes.definition: Have the specific holdout cases chosen by a party with no stake in the result and no access to model outputs, ideally outcome-blind, so the selection itself cannot encode the designer's or evaluator's hindsight about which cases the model will get right.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the selecting party gains outcome knowledge or a stake in the result

pros.claim: An uninvolved selector breaks the link between the designer's outcome knowledge and which cases appear, closing the selection leg of designer leakage
pros.example: a librarian draws cases by a pre-registered rule from the post-cutoff pool, with no view of outcomes

cons.claim: A naive blind selector may pick degenerate or trivially-answerable cases, trading leakage control for low task quality
cons.example: random blind sampling yields ten near-identical events that test one narrow skill

failure_modes: the designer hand-picks cases under the guise of blindness
the selector can see model outputs or outcomes
acceptance_tests: cases are drawn by an uninvolved, outcome-blind party following a pre-registered selection rule
revisit_triggers: the selector is found to share interests with the evaluator
selected cases are trivially answerable

nodes.definition: Screen every feature, prompt field, and context document for label leakage: information that is a proxy for, or only available because of, the outcome (post-outcome timestamps, outcome-conditioned text, identifiers that encode the result), and remove or quarantine such legitimacy violations before the case is finalized.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new feature, context document, or data source is added to a case

pros.claim: Kaufman et al. formalize legitimacy: a feature is leaking if it would be unavailable at genuine prediction time; screening enforces that boundary
pros.example: a news snippet dated after the event that already names the outcome is quarantined from the prompt

cons.claim: Subtle leakage is hard to catch: an innocuous-looking field can be a near-deterministic outcome proxy
cons.example: a record ID assigned only to firms that later filed for bankruptcy silently encodes the label

failure_modes: a post-outcome document leaks into the context
an identifier or timestamp encodes the result
acceptance_tests: every feature is available strictly at prediction time and none is shown to proxy the outcome
revisit_triggers: a new data source is added to a case
an audit finds a high-leverage feature correlates near-perfectly with the label

nodes.definition: Attach an as-of timestamp and source provenance to every feature value so each can be proven to have existed and been knowable strictly before the event's resolution, turning leakage screening from a judgment call into a checkable as-of date comparison.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a feature's provenance or as-of date is missing or disputed

pros.claim: Point-in-time as-of dating makes 'available at prediction time' an auditable fact, the operational core of the legitimacy criterion
pros.example: each feature carries the date it was first publicly available, all strictly before the resolution date

cons.claim: Point-in-time reconstruction is laborious and many real datasets silently back-fill revised values
cons.example: an economic series is revised after the fact, so its stored value is not what was knowable then

failure_modes: a back-filled (revised) value is used as if it were point-in-time
a feature lacks any as-of date
acceptance_tests: every feature value carries an as-of date strictly before its event's resolution date
revisit_triggers: a feature is found to be a revised/back-filled value
provenance for a feature cannot be reconstructed

nodes.definition: Actively probe whether the model can reproduce the held-out outcome or recognize the test item from pretraining: ask it to complete, recite, or date the event before the evaluation, and treat any successful recitation as evidence the case is contaminated and must be dropped or quarantined.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the probe protocol or the model version changes

pros.claim: Sainz et al. recommend exactly this: measure contamination per benchmark by checking whether the model can reproduce held instances
pros.example: prompting the model with the case stem and finding it completes the true outcome flags contamination directly

cons.claim: Probes have false negatives: a model may exploit contaminated knowledge without verbatim recitation, so a clean probe is not a clean bill
cons.example: Magar & Schwartz show exploitation can occur without reproducible memorization, so probes under-detect

failure_modes: a recitable case kept because the probe was too narrow
probe run on a different model version than the one evaluated
acceptance_tests: every retained case passes a recitation probe (model cannot reproduce the outcome) on the exact evaluated model version
revisit_triggers: the model version under test changes
an exploited-but-not-recited contamination case is discovered

nodes.definition: Establish a baseline that measures pure recall versus genuine prediction: give the model the case with and without the discriminating pre-cutoff context, so that score gains attributable to memorized knowledge can be separated from gains attributable to actual forecasting skill.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the baseline conditions or the discriminating-context definition change

pros.claim: A recall baseline operationalizes Magar & Schwartz's memorization-vs-exploitation split, giving a quantitative handle on how much score is leakage
pros.example: if the no-context score already matches the with-context score, the 'skill' is memorized recall

cons.claim: Designing a truly information-free recall condition is hard; residual cues can leak the answer into the baseline too
cons.example: stripping context still leaves a distinctive entity name that the model has memorized

failure_modes: baseline still leaks the answer through residual cues
recall and prediction conditions differ on more than the target information
acceptance_tests: the recall-only baseline isolates memorized recall from forecasting skill within a stated margin
revisit_triggers: the discriminating-context definition changes
the recall baseline scores implausibly high

nodes.definition: Quantify the leakage that remains after all controls: combine probe hit rates, the recall baseline, and feature-screen residuals into an explicit residual-leakage estimate with an uncertainty band, and attach it to every reported result so consumers can discount the score accordingly.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any control's measured effectiveness or a probe hit-rate changes materially

pros.claim: An explicit residual estimate replaces the false binary 'leak-free vs leaky' with an honest quantified remainder consumers can act on
pros.example: reporting 'estimated residual leakage 5-12%, discount accuracy accordingly' instead of claiming zero leakage

cons.claim: The residual estimate is itself uncertain and can be falsely reassuring if its own assumptions are wrong
cons.example: a low residual estimate built on an under-powered probe gives unwarranted confidence

failure_modes: residual leakage reported as zero
the estimate's own uncertainty omitted, implying false precision
acceptance_tests: a residual-leakage estimate with an uncertainty band accompanies every reported metric
revisit_triggers: a control's measured effectiveness changes
a post-hoc leak exceeds the residual band

nodes.definition: Pre-compute the holdout size needed to detect the target effect given that post-cutoff events are scarce, and reconcile the leakage-driven shrinkage of the usable pool with the power requirement, so the holdout is neither contaminated nor too small to conclude anything.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the target effect size, scoring rule, or the usable-pool size changes

pros.claim: Pre-computing power before freezing prevents the common failure of a perfectly clean but uninformatively tiny holdout
pros.example: power analysis shows 40 post-cutoff cases are needed to detect a 10-point gap, so the pool is sized accordingly

cons.claim: Enlarging the pool to gain power can force inclusion of borderline or weaker post-cutoff events, trading purity for size
cons.example: reaching the required n means admitting events whose post-cutoff status is only marginally established

failure_modes: holdout too small to detect the target effect
power chased by admitting contaminated cases
acceptance_tests: the holdout meets a pre-computed minimum-detectable-effect at the registered metric
revisit_triggers: the target effect size is revised
the usable post-cutoff pool shrinks below the power requirement

nodes.definition: Enforce single-use hygiene: the holdout is scored once, never iterated against, never used to tune prompts or thresholds, and is retired after use, because repeated evaluation against the same holdout re-introduces leakage through adaptive overfitting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the holdout is requested for a second evaluation or for tuning

pros.claim: One-time use closes the adaptive-overfitting channel: re-running against the same holdout leaks via the analyst's reaction to prior scores
pros.example: a team that retunes a prompt after a failing run has leaked the holdout into their prompt, even though the model never 'saw' new data

cons.claim: Single-use is costly: a fresh leakage-controlled holdout must be built for every new evaluation cycle
cons.example: each model release needs a newly assembled post-cutoff holdout, which is expensive to source

failure_modes: the holdout reused to tune a prompt
scores from a prior run inform the next design without retiring the set
acceptance_tests: the holdout is scored exactly once and retired; no tuning decision references its results
revisit_triggers: a second evaluation against the same holdout is requested
prompt tuning is observed to reference holdout scores

nodes.definition: Deliver the frozen holdout to the model under a sealed, blind protocol: the evaluator runs the model without the ability to inspect or amend cases, and outputs are captured before any outcome is revealed, so the act of evaluation cannot itself introduce hindsight or selection.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the delivery or output-capture protocol changes

pros.claim: Sealing the cases and capturing outputs before outcomes are revealed prevents the evaluator from quietly dropping hard cases
pros.example: model outputs are hashed and stored before the real-world outcomes resolve, so nothing can be retrofitted

cons.claim: A fully sealed pipeline reduces the evaluator's ability to catch a genuine case-construction bug mid-run
cons.example: a malformed prompt cannot be fixed without breaking the seal and logging a deviation

failure_modes: the evaluator edits cases during the run
outputs captured only after outcomes are known
acceptance_tests: all model outputs are captured and hashed before any outcome resolves, with no evaluator amendment
revisit_triggers: the delivery protocol changes
an output is found to have been captured post-outcome

nodes.definition: Run a standing, independent leakage audit over the finished holdout and its evaluation: re-check cutoffs, re-run probes, re-screen features, and verify pre-registration integrity, producing a sign-off (or a list of defects) before any result is published.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any control is changed, or a published result is challenged on leakage grounds

pros.claim: An independent standing audit catches control failures the designer is blind to, closing the loop on the analyst-as-leak problem
pros.example: the auditor re-runs the recitation probe on the exact evaluated model and finds two contaminated cases the designer missed

cons.claim: Audits add latency and can become a rubber stamp if the auditor lacks independence or teeth
cons.example: an under-resourced audit signs off without re-running the expensive probes

failure_modes: the audit is not independent of the designer
controls passed at design time but drifted by evaluation time
acceptance_tests: an independent auditor re-verifies every control and signs off or files defects before publication
revisit_triggers: a control is modified after sign-off
a published result is challenged on leakage grounds

nodes.definition: Maintain a transparent, append-only log of every deviation from the pre-registration (dropped cases, reworded questions, metric changes) with timestamp and justification, so post-registration changes are visible and cannot covertly tune the design toward the outcome.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any deviation from the registered plan occurs

pros.claim: An append-only deviation log preserves the credibility of pre-registration even when changes are unavoidable, per the preregistration revolution
pros.example: dropping three contaminated cases is logged with the probe evidence and timestamp, not done silently

cons.claim: A deviation log can be abused to legitimize so many changes that the pre-registration becomes meaningless
cons.example: twenty post-hoc deviations effectively rebuild the design after seeing results

failure_modes: a change made without a logged justification
deviations so numerous the registration is gutted
acceptance_tests: every post-registration change is recorded append-only with timestamp and justification
revisit_triggers: a silent (unlogged) deviation is discovered
the count of deviations exceeds a credibility threshold

nodes.definition: State and enforce the core finding: 'the model/designer did not see this case during design' is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for a leakage-free evaluation; a result may be published as leakage-controlled only if BOTH the pretraining channel and the designer-knowledge channel are demonstrably controlled, not merely the design-time visibility.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a claim of leakage-freedom rests on design-time blindness alone

pros.claim: Making the sufficiency gap explicit prevents the most common evaluation error: declaring a test clean because nobody peeked, while the model memorized the answer
pros.example: a benchmark called 'held-out' because the team kept it private still leaks if the model pretrained on the underlying events

cons.claim: Holding results to the both-channels bar will block some otherwise interesting evaluations from claiming leakage-freedom
cons.example: a compelling result must be downgraded to 'leakage-suspected' because the designer channel was not fully controlled

failure_modes: a result published as leak-free on design-time blindness alone
only one of the two channels is controlled but the claim is unqualified
acceptance_tests: no result is labeled leakage-controlled unless both the pretraining and designer-knowledge channels are demonstrably controlled
revisit_triggers: a published claim rests on visibility alone
an audit finds one channel uncontrolled behind a leak-free claim

nodes.definition: Emit a structured disclosure that travels with every reported result: the confirmed cutoff, which channels were controlled and how, the probe and audit findings, the residual-leakage estimate, and the deviation log, so a consumer can independently judge the evaluation's leakage standing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any control, residual estimate, or deviation changes after disclosure

pros.claim: A disclosure that carries cutoff, controls, probes, residual estimate, and deviations lets consumers replicate the leakage judgment rather than trust it
pros.example: the result ships with 'cutoff 2024-03, both channels controlled, residual 5-12%, two logged deviations'

cons.claim: Disclosure can be gamed by burying weak control coverage in dense boilerplate that few readers parse
cons.example: a long disclosure that technically lists every channel but hides that the designer channel was uncontrolled

failure_modes: a result published without its leakage disclosure
disclosure omits the residual estimate or the deviation log
acceptance_tests: every published result carries a structured disclosure naming cutoff, both channels, probes, residual, and deviations
revisit_triggers: a control changes after disclosure
a consumer cannot reconstruct the leakage judgment from the disclosure

edges.why_related: a probe hit feeds back to drop the case from the post-cutoff pool
the audit can revise the effective cutoff if near-boundary probing reveals a later one
as-of dating of features constrains which post-cutoff events can be fully reconstructed
the power-driven target size constrains the blind selector's sampling rule
a high recall baseline is direct evidence the necessary-not-sufficient gate must block a leak-free claim
reusing or re-tuning the holdout would generate deviations the log must capture
temporal look-ahead and feature label leakage are two forms of the same prediction-time-availability violation
the audit checklist is the threat model re-applied independently at the end
strict post-cutoff sourcing shrinks the pool, conflicting with the sample size needed for statistical power
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: purity dominates: never admit borderline-cutoff cases to reach power; instead lower the target effect or report an under-powered result with widened confidence intervals

edges.why_related: post-cutoff events can still be designer-leaked through which post-cutoff cases the designer picks
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: post-cutoff timing controls the model channel but not the designer channel; require BLIND_SELECTION on the post-cutoff pool so neither channel is left open

edges.why_related: fully blind random selection can produce too few or degenerate cases to satisfy the power requirement
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: constrain the blind selector with a pre-registered stratified rule so blindness yields enough informative cases to meet power without hand-picking

edges.why_related: one-time-use hygiene conflicts with the temptation to reuse a scarce holdout to accumulate statistical power
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: single-use forbids reusing the holdout to chase power; build a larger or fresh holdout rather than re-scoring the retired one

conflict_axes.name: purity_vs_statistical_power
conflict_axes.description: Strict post-cutoff sourcing maximizes leakage control but shrinks the pool below the size needed to detect the target effect.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lower the target effect or widen intervals rather than admitting borderline-cutoff cases

conflict_axes.name: pretraining_channel_vs_designer_channel
conflict_axes.description: Controlling pretraining ingestion does not control designer hindsight, and vice versa; both must be closed independently.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require demonstrable control of BOTH channels before any leak-free claim

conflict_axes.name: designer_expertise_vs_designer_blindness
conflict_axes.description: The domain expertise needed to build a good forecasting task carries the very outcome hindsight that must be excluded.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: separate task authoring from blind case selection by an uninvolved party

conflict_axes.name: preregistration_rigidity_vs_correctability
conflict_axes.description: Freezing the design prevents post-hoc tuning but blocks fixing a genuine flaw discovered after registration.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow only append-only logged deviations with justification

conflict_axes.name: memorization_vs_exploitation
conflict_axes.description: A model can ingest a contaminated item yet not exploit it; treating all memorization as fatal over-excludes, ignoring it under-detects.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use a recall baseline to measure exploitation, not just memorization

conflict_axes.name: probe_sensitivity_vs_false_negatives
conflict_axes.description: Recitation probes detect verbatim memorization but miss non-recited exploitation, so a clean probe can falsely reassure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pair probes with a recall baseline and report residual leakage, never zero

conflict_axes.name: single_use_vs_holdout_reuse
conflict_axes.description: One-time use prevents adaptive overfitting but forces rebuilding a scarce holdout for every cycle.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build fresh holdouts; never re-score a retired one to chase power

conflict_axes.name: point_in_time_fidelity_vs_data_availability
conflict_axes.description: Proving features were knowable before the outcome requires point-in-time data that many sources silently back-fill.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require an as-of date per feature; quarantine values that cannot be reconstructed

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_completeness_vs_readability
conflict_axes.description: A complete leakage disclosure is long and can bury weak control coverage that few readers parse.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lead with a channel-by-channel control summary and residual estimate, detail in appendix

edge_cases.description: A held-out case is a famous historical event the model memorized verbatim during pretraining, so a high score reflects recall, not prediction.
edge_cases.trigger: a pre-cutoff famous outcome is used as a test item
edge_cases.mitigation: restrict to strictly post-cutoff events and drop any case the model can recite

edge_cases.description: The designer, knowing which firms later failed, quietly over-samples failures into a nominally balanced holdout.
edge_cases.trigger: the designer selects cases while knowing outcomes
edge_cases.mitigation: have an uninvolved, outcome-blind party draw cases by a pre-registered rule

edge_cases.description: The team declares a benchmark 'held-out' because they kept it private, while the underlying events were in pretraining.
edge_cases.trigger: a leak-free claim rests on design-time blindness alone
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the both-channels bar: control pretraining AND designer channels, not just visibility

edge_cases.description: Random k-fold cross-validation is used on time-ordered evaluation data, leaking future periods into the training side.
edge_cases.trigger: random CV applied to time-ordered data
edge_cases.mitigation: split strictly by time with an embargo gap and forbid look-ahead features

edge_cases.description: A context document dated after the event already names the outcome and is fed into the model's prompt.
edge_cases.trigger: a post-outcome document leaks into the case context
edge_cases.mitigation: screen every feature for as-of date strictly before resolution; quarantine post-outcome text

edge_cases.description: An identifier or back-filled timestamp silently encodes the label (e.g. an ID assigned only to firms that later failed).
edge_cases.trigger: a feature is a near-deterministic outcome proxy
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the legitimacy criterion and point-in-time reconstruction to every feature

edge_cases.description: A recitation probe comes back clean, yet the model still exploits contaminated knowledge without reproducing it verbatim.
edge_cases.trigger: a clean probe is taken as proof of zero contamination
edge_cases.mitigation: pair probes with a recall baseline and report a non-zero residual-leakage estimate

edge_cases.description: After a failing run, the team re-tunes the prompt and re-scores the same holdout, leaking it via adaptive overfitting.
edge_cases.trigger: the holdout is reused to tune prompts or thresholds
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce single-use and retire the holdout after one scoring

edge_cases.description: The usable post-cutoff pool is too small to detect the target effect, so the clean holdout is uninformative.
edge_cases.trigger: leakage control shrinks the pool below the power requirement
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-compute power; lower the target effect or widen intervals rather than admitting contaminated cases

edge_cases.description: A vendor-stated cutoff is trusted, but continued pretraining or retrieval injects post-cutoff knowledge the date does not capture.
edge_cases.trigger: the cutoff is taken from documentation without empirical probing
edge_cases.mitigation: empirically corroborate the cutoff against near-boundary events and account for retrieval

edge_cases.description: Cases are silently dropped after results are seen, with no record, quietly tuning the design toward a flattering outcome.
edge_cases.trigger: post-registration changes are made without a deviation log
edge_cases.mitigation: record every change append-only with timestamp and justification before publication

edge_cases.description: The evaluation audit is performed by the same person who designed the holdout, so designer blind spots survive into publication.
edge_cases.trigger: the leakage audit is not independent of the designer
edge_cases.mitigation: assign an independent auditor to re-run probes and re-screen features before sign-off

workflow.description: Enumerate every leakage channel treating the system as model PLUS designer; map each channel to an owning control.
workflow.gate: every channel has an owning control and a residual-risk note

workflow.description: Determine and empirically corroborate the model and designer knowledge cutoff.
workflow.gate: the cutoff is documented and probed against near-boundary events

workflow.description: Stand up controls for both the pretraining and designer-knowledge channels.
workflow.gate: both channels have an assigned, instantiated control

workflow.description: Assemble candidate events whose outcomes resolved strictly after the confirmed cutoff.
workflow.gate: every pooled event resolves strictly after the cutoff

workflow.description: Freeze cases, question wording, metric, and analysis plan in a timestamped tamper-evident registration before any output is seen.
workflow.gate: cases, metric, and analysis plan are hashed and timestamped

workflow.description: Have an uninvolved, outcome-blind party draw the final cases by the pre-registered rule.
workflow.gate: selection is made by an uninvolved outcome-blind party

workflow.description: Screen every feature and context document for label leakage and attach as-of provenance.
workflow.gate: every feature is knowable strictly before resolution

workflow.description: Probe the exact evaluated model for recitation of each held-out outcome; quarantine any recitable case.
workflow.gate: no retained case is recitable by the evaluated model

workflow.description: Verify the holdout meets the pre-computed minimum-detectable-effect and set the recall baseline.
Combine probe, baseline, and feature-screen residuals into a residual-leakage estimate with an uncertainty band.
workflow.gate: a residual estimate with an uncertainty band exists

workflow.description: Deliver the sealed holdout, run the model once under hygiene rules, and capture outputs before outcomes resolve.
workflow.gate: outputs are captured and hashed before any outcome resolves

workflow.description: Run the independent leakage audit, log deviations, and publish only with the structured leakage disclosure.
workflow.gate: an independent audit signs off and a disclosure ships with the result

priority_rationale: THREAT_MODEL and CUTOFF_DETERMINATION are foundational; the two channel-control nodes and POST_CUTOFF_HOLDOUT establish the core guarantees; pre-registration, blind selection, feature screening, and probes operationalize them; residual estimation, hygiene, audit, and the necessary-not-sufficient gate close the method before disclosure.

dominance_rules.rule: CUTOFF_DETERMINATION must be confirmed before any case is admitted to the post-cutoff pool
dominance_rules.rationale: every post-cutoff guarantee is anchored to the confirmed cutoff; an unconfirmed cutoff invalidates the whole pool
dominance_rules.trigger: cases are sourced before the cutoff is empirically corroborated
dominance_rules.action: block pool assembly until the cutoff is confirmed

dominance_rules.rule: Both the pretraining and designer-knowledge channels must be controlled before any result is labeled leakage-controlled
dominance_rules.rationale: design-time blindness is necessary but not sufficient; one open channel leaks regardless of the other
dominance_rules.trigger: a leak-free claim rests on only one channel or on visibility alone
dominance_rules.action: block the leak-free label until both channels are demonstrably controlled

dominance_rules.rule: Case selection and metrics must be pre-registered before any model output or outcome is observed
dominance_rules.rationale: selecting or scoring after seeing results reintroduces researcher degrees of freedom
dominance_rules.trigger: metric or case set chosen after an output is seen
dominance_rules.action: reject the result and require a fresh pre-registration

dominance_rules.rule: Final case selection must be performed by an uninvolved outcome-blind party
dominance_rules.rationale: a designer who knows outcomes leaks them through which cases appear
dominance_rules.trigger: the designer hand-picks the final cases
dominance_rules.action: void the selection and re-draw blindly

dominance_rules.rule: Every feature must pass the legitimacy (as-of date) check before its case is finalized
dominance_rules.rationale: a feature unavailable at prediction time is label leakage
dominance_rules.trigger: a feature lacks an as-of date strictly before resolution
dominance_rules.action: quarantine the feature or drop the case

dominance_rules.rule: Any case the evaluated model can recite must be dropped or quarantined
dominance_rules.rationale: a recitable outcome is memorized, not predicted
dominance_rules.trigger: a recitation probe succeeds on a retained case
dominance_rules.action: drop the case from the scored set

dominance_rules.rule: Residual leakage must be reported as a non-zero estimate with an uncertainty band; zero-leakage claims are forbidden
dominance_rules.rationale: probes under-detect non-recited exploitation, so zero leakage cannot be asserted
dominance_rules.trigger: a result claims zero or unstated residual leakage
dominance_rules.action: require a residual estimate with its uncertainty before publication

dominance_rules.rule: The holdout must be scored exactly once and retired; reuse for tuning is prohibited
dominance_rules.rationale: repeated evaluation leaks the holdout through adaptive overfitting
dominance_rules.trigger: a second scoring or a tuning decision references holdout results
dominance_rules.action: retire the holdout and require a fresh one

dominance_rules.rule: The leakage audit must be independent of the designer and complete before publication
dominance_rules.rationale: a self-audit preserves the designer's blind spots
dominance_rules.trigger: the auditor is the designer or lacks independence
dominance_rules.action: assign an independent auditor and block publication until sign-off

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not source the candidate pool before confirming the cutoff; a revised cutoff invalidates every sourced case
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-sourcing the entire pool after the effective cutoff is found to be later than assumed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not let the designer pick cases; reconstructing a blind selection after the fact requires discarding the contaminated set
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the holdout after a hindsight-laden selection is discovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize features without as-of provenance; retrofitting point-in-time dating forces re-screening every case
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-screening all features after a back-filled value is found to leak the label

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run probes on a different model version than the one evaluated; a version change voids the probe evidence
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the full contamination probe suite after the evaluated model version changes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not choose the metric or threshold after seeing outputs; post-hoc metric changes require a fresh pre-registration and holdout
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scrapping a result and rebuilding the holdout because the metric was tuned to the answer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not reuse the holdout to chase statistical power; a reused holdout is leaked and cannot be un-leaked
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discarding adaptive-overfit results and assembling a fresh holdout under deadline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not make post-registration changes without a deviation log; unlogged edits force re-justifying the whole design
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing the change history to defend a challenged result

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not publish before the independent audit signs off; a post-publication leak finding forces a retraction
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting a published result after an independent audit finds an uncontrolled channel

iteration_protocol.trigger: near-boundary probing reveals the effective cutoff is later than assumed
iteration_protocol.action: revise CUTOFF_DETERMINATION and re-source POST_CUTOFF_HOLDOUT against the corrected date

iteration_protocol.trigger: a recitation probe shows the evaluated model can reproduce a held-out outcome
iteration_protocol.action: drop the case in CONTAMINATION_PROBES and re-estimate residual leakage

iteration_protocol.trigger: a result is claimed leakage-free on design-time blindness alone
iteration_protocol.action: apply the NECESSARY_NOT_SUFFICIENT gate and verify both channels are controlled before any leak-free label

iteration_protocol.trigger: selected cases are found to correlate with known outcomes
iteration_protocol.action: void the selection and re-draw blindly in BLIND_SELECTION under the pre-registered rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: a feature is found to be a back-filled or post-outcome value
iteration_protocol.action: quarantine it in LABEL_LEAKAGE_SCREEN and reconstruct point-in-time provenance in FEATURE_PROVENANCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: the usable post-cutoff pool shrinks below the power requirement
iteration_protocol.action: lower the target effect or widen intervals in POWER_AND_SAMPLE rather than admitting contaminated cases

iteration_protocol.trigger: the holdout is requested for a second evaluation or for tuning
iteration_protocol.action: retire it under HOLDOUT_HYGIENE and assemble a fresh holdout instead of re-scoring

iteration_protocol.trigger: an independent audit files a leakage defect after sign-off was assumed
iteration_protocol.action: log the deviation in PREREG_DEVIATION_LOG and update the disclosure before publication
